action_history.rationale: Step 0 of a 10-experiment campaign with 5 initial points in 1D. Full budget remains so we have room for balanced exploration-exploitation. log_ei is the ideal default for batch_size=1: it will naturally explore uncertain regions while leveraging the promising signal near x≈3.8 (y≈1.0). Standard Matérn-2.5 kernel with low noise floor is appropriate for this 1D problem with unknown noise characteristics. No evidence yet to warrant non-default model choices.

Step 2 of 10, 9 experiments remain (90% budget). Only 6 data points in 1D — still early stage. log_ei is the natural choice for batch_size=1: it will balance exploring uncertain regions (e.g., gaps in x-coverage or near boundaries) with exploiting the promising peak near x≈3.8 (y≈0.998). Model diagnostics from step 1 confirmed good calibration with Matérn-2.5 and low noise floor, so no changes needed. No plateau concern after just 1 optimization step.

Step 2 diagnostics flagged a critical acquisition optimizer failure: log_ei pushed the candidate to the domain boundary (x≈10) due to numerical flattening of the log-transformed surface, missing clear peaks near x≈0.5–4. Switching to UCB avoids this issue — its acquisition surface is well-behaved without log transforms. Beta=1.5 provides balanced exploration-exploitation appropriate for 80% remaining budget. The GP model itself (Matérn-2.5, low noise, single_task) was confirmed well-calibrated by LOO-CV, so no model changes are needed. The goal is to let the acquisition optimizer properly identify and sample promising regions rather than getting trapped at boundary artifacts.

Step 3 diagnostics confirmed UCB(β=1.5) resolved the acquisition optimizer failure from Step 2 (log_ei boundary artifact at x=10). The candidate correctly aligned with the acquisition peak near x≈2. Model is well-calibrated (LOO-CV residuals within 1σ band). With 70% budget remaining and only 3 BO steps completed (no plateau concern yet), continuing with the same balanced UCB(β=1.5) strategy is appropriate — it provides good exploration-exploitation balance while avoiding the log_ei numerical issues. No model changes needed; Matérn-2.5 and low noise floor are confirmed suitable for this 1D landscape.

Step 4 of 10, 6 remaining (60% budget). Best y≈1.0 found near x≈3.8 in initial data, unchanged through 4 BO steps — but no plateau escalation yet (need 5+ steps). UCB(β=1.5) successfully resolved the log_ei boundary artifact from Step 2, and with 9 data points now (vs 6 when the artifact occurred), log_ei should behave properly. Switching back to log_ei for its natural exploration-exploitation balance — it will focus on regions with genuine expected improvement rather than repeatedly targeting the same UCB peak near x≈2. Model confirmed well-calibrated (LOO-CV within 1σ), so keeping Matérn-2.5 with low noise floor.

Plateau escalation Step A: best y≈1.0 unchanged for 5 BO steps, so switching to UCB(β=2.5) to probe beyond the current basin near x≈3.8. log_ei has failed 2 out of 3 times in this campaign (Steps 2 and 5) due to numerical instability pushing candidates to boundary/trough regions — UCB avoids this entirely and worked correctly in Steps 3-4. Adopting Matérn-1.5 and medium noise floor per Step 5 diagnostics: LOO-CV residuals at points 5-6 exceed the uncertainty band, suggesting local roughness that benefits from a rougher kernel and slight regularization. With 50% budget remaining (5 experiments), β=2.5 provides meaningful exploration of under-sampled regions while still weighting toward plausible improvement.

6-step plateau with best y≈1.0 at x≈3.8 unchanged. Step A escalation (UCB β=2.5) at Step 5 passed diagnostics but did not break the plateau — the candidate targeted x≈2, still within the heavily sampled x≈0.5–4 basin. Escalating to Step B: UCB(β=5.0) to push exploration into the severely undersampled x≈4–10 region (only 1 data point at x=10). The higher β will weight uncertainty more heavily, directing the candidate toward information-sparse regions that could harbor an undiscovered optimum. With 4 experiments remaining (40% budget), there is still room to explore now and exploit in the final 1–2 steps if a new promising region is found. Keeping Matérn-1.5 and medium noise from Step 5 — diagnostics confirmed good calibration with these settings. log_ei is excluded due to repeated numerical failures (2/3 attempts).

Budget = 3, must exploit. Best y = 0.999972 at x ≈ 3.8 — essentially at the optimum with negligible room for improvement. The 7-step 'plateau' reflects convergence to the true optimum rather than being stuck in a basin. log_ei is excluded due to 2/3 numerical failure rate in this campaign. UCB(β=0.5) provides controlled exploitation near the known best region. Reverting to Matérn-2.5 and low noise for sharper model predictions near the peak — the earlier switch to Matérn-1.5/medium noise was for exploration phases that are now over. With 3 remaining shots, all should focus on confirming and refining the optimum near x ≈ 3.8.

Budget = 2, must exploit. Best y = 0.999999 near x ≈ 3.8 — effectively at the optimum. log_ei is excluded due to 2/3 numerical failure rate throughout this campaign (boundary artifacts at Steps 2 and 5); with only 2 experiments left, we cannot risk another wasted shot. UCB(β=0.3) provides strong exploitation and has worked reliably every time in this campaign. Matérn-2.5 and low noise give sharp model predictions near the peak for precise refinement. The goal is to confirm the optimum and potentially squeeze out the last fractional improvement near x ≈ 3.8.

This is the FINAL experiment (budget=1). Best y=0.999999 near x≈3.8 — essentially at the theoretical maximum of 1.0. UCB(β=0.1) provides maximum exploitation to target the precise optimum location. Using UCB rather than log_ei because log_ei suffered numerical failures in 2 out of 3 attempts during this campaign (Steps 2 and 5), producing boundary artifacts and trough candidates — we cannot risk a wasted final shot. UCB has worked reliably every time. β=0.1 (well below the 0.3 threshold for final shots) ensures the candidate will be placed at the GP posterior mean maximum, which should be very close to x≈3.8 where the best observation lies. Matérn-2.5 with low noise provides the sharpest possible model predictions near the peak for precise refinement of the last fractional improvement.
